title: SilenceSketch
summary: A local browser audio editor that visualizes long pauses, lets users keep or remove each proposed cut, and exports the tightened result as WAV.
audience: Podcasters, video creators, interviewers and anyone cleaning spoken recordings.
problem: Removing dead air from speech recordings is repetitive, but fully automatic cutting can damage intentional pauses. Users need a fast way to see proposed cuts and keep exceptions before exporting.
difference: SilenceSketch is a zero-upload, no-account browser workflow focused on inspect-adjust-export: it visualizes detected silence, recalculates instantly as sensitivity changes, lets users veto individual cuts, and renders a real WAV output locally.
limitations: The first version exports WAV rather than preserving the original codec.
Very long recordings consume browser memory because decoding and rendering happen locally.
Silence detection is energy-based and does not distinguish room tone from intentional ambience.

alternatives.name: QuietCut
alternatives.difference: QuietCut is a fuller desktop/video product with automated cutting and paid tiers; SilenceSketch is a tiny zero-install browser workspace for quickly reviewing and vetoing pause cuts before WAV export.

alternatives.name: AutoClipper
alternatives.difference: AutoClipper is a full local AI video editing stack with transcription and smart cropping; SilenceSketch deliberately avoids model downloads and focuses on one fast spoken-audio cleanup interaction.
